title: What Did They Mean? How LLMs Resolve Ambiguous Social Situations across Perspectives and Roles

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model responses to identical ambiguous interpersonal scenarios using either first-person or third-person framing to measure how the narrator's position affects the model's interpretive closure.
Evaluating whether models exhibit 'narrative alignment' by confirming and extending the user's tentative hypothesis in an ambiguous situation rather than preserving uncertainty.

Analyzing whether models distribute credibility, sympathy, and the benefit of the doubt asymmetrically by comparing responses across hierarchical domains (teacher-student, workplace) versus egalitarian domains (friendships, early-stage romance).
